app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.

Lists supported metadata embeds, contextual ordering directions and global timing method names by resource path. Game detail supplies per-game timing support. No upstream collection or account request is made.

Reads one native /runs page, preserving native attempts, statuses, timings, attribution references, selected game metadata and pagination. A run need not be a current leaderboard record. Entity discovery and every-row membership checks prevent ignored filters from returning unrelated runs. Freeform comments/reviewer/video text, split content and embedded rules/community/media fields are excluded. Account-scoped user/guest/examiner selectors and player/profile embeds are not exposed. No local ranking, collection loop or synthetic cursor is added.

Returns one native run's game/category/level identity, timestamps, timing values, status and attribution references. Native nulls and metadata embed wrappers remain intact. Freeform comments/reviewer/video text, split content and embedded rules/community/media fields are excluded; media and account/profile resources are not fetched. A native404 is not an empty success.
